newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Yieh Loong plans T$50-60 bln mall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Yieh Loong plans T$50-60 bln mall.

text.p: Taiwan's Yieh Loong steel group said on Tuesday it planned to seek business partners to build a T$50-60 billion giant shopping mall in the southern Kaohsiung city, pending government approval.

The mall -- which would include shipping arcades, movie theatres and hotels -- would begin construction in 1999 if the government gives the go-ahead, Yieh Loong spokesman Yang Sen-lung told Reuters by telephone.
"We want to develop our land in northern Kaohsiung for commercial use because right now all the big department stores and shopping districts are in southern Kaohsiung," Yang said.
"The fact that northern Kaohsiung is less developed means it has more potential," he said. "And we are definitely talking about potential because our project will not be completed before 2000."
Yang said the northern Kaohsiung land, about 240,000 square feet in area, is owned jointly by Yieh Loong and Kaohsiung city government.
Half of the land would be used to build the mall while the other half would be turned into a public park and recreation centre, Yang said.
Yieh Loong said it would seek partners to finance the project after the Kaohsiung government granted formal approval.
"We expect the approval to come at some point in 1998," Yang said.
Several other Taiwan companies -- some with government backing -- have been planning shopping centre projects in a bid to capture the growing consumer strength of the island's affluent population.
Food giant President Enterprises Corp has said it planned to invest more than T$20 billion to build a shopping mall in the southern city of Tainan.

The government is currently constructing a T$13 billion mall in northern Chungli city and said it would lend T$11.921 billion to help finance a T$23.96 billion private mall in Taipei by a consortium led by Core Pacific Group.
